title: Causal Inference: What If
inspection: Selected sections 6.2–6.3 printed pp.78–81 and 8.1 printed pp.109–110. Not a complete-book reading.
originalRetention: Downloaded and inspected in temporary workspace, not republished as a complete copyrighted book in this repository.
shortExcerpt: An association created as a result of the process by which individuals are selected into the analysis is referred to as selection bias.
reviewerParaphrase: Common causes can produce association without a direct causal effect. Restricting an analysis to a common effect or its descendant may open a noncausal path. Selection of only prominent scandals can therefore undermine inferences from apparent network patterns.
limit: A methodological analogy, not evidence for any particular explanation of a case and not an estimated causal effect.
